reports.title: Lineage, Inc. Reports Third-Quarter 2026 Financial Results

lines: Lineage expects full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $1.25 to $1.27 billion and Adjusted FFO ("AFFO") per share of $2.86 to $2.98.
EBITDA guidance ($1,260M) would adjust to $1,287M, above the midpoint of initial 2026 Adj.

desk.headline: Revenue down 1% to $1.36bn, slight miss; AFFO/share falls to $0.73; 2026 outlook range narrowed
results: Revenue slipped 1.2% to $1.36bn, just under the $1.37bn estimate; same-warehouse revenue edged up 0.4%.
Net loss widened to $173m ($0.68 a share, vs a $0.23 loss expected), mainly due to a $105m loss on destroyed property and higher interest costs ($92m vs $68m).
Adjusted EBITDA fell 7% to $317m and AFFO per share 14% to $0.73, as power costs jumped 13% at same warehouses.
Occupancy kept improving: same-warehouse physical occupancy rose to 76.2% from 75.1%, though storage revenue per pallet fell 2.2%.
The transport-heavy Global Integrated Solutions unit was weakest, with NOI down 14% to $56m; the $0.5325 quarterly dividend was kept.

guidance.summary: Lineage now expects 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $1.25–1.27bn and AFFO of $2.86–2.98 a share. The AFFO range was tightened from $2.80–3.05 (August call) around a similar midpoint; it said Q4 pressures were built into the update.

points: The CEO said core trends kept stabilising, with occupancy up year on year for a second quarter, a sign customer stock levels have normalised.
Late in the quarter, much higher oil prices, tight trucking capacity and tariff uncertainty hurt, especially in the integrated solutions business.
Management expects those pressures to last into Q4 but called them cyclical, not a change in direction.
call.source: CEO comments in the press release (Exhibit 99.1); no coverage of the 10 Nov call found

watch: Whether fuel, trucking and tariff headwinds ease in Q4 as management expects.
Occupancy versus pricing: occupancy is rising but storage revenue per pallet is still falling.
Debt and interest costs, with long-term debt up to $6.8bn from $6.1bn at end-2025.
